title: Shadowsocks HarmonyOS 5.4.0 Android parity · 需求层决策说明
conclusion: The Android mobile app at v5.3.5-nightly is the parity target. Review the scope, the journey set and the acceptance bar.

abbreviations.ASCII: American standard code for information interchange

decisions.question: Is the Android v5.3.5-nightly mobile app the correct parity target?
decisions.reason: The reversed requirements, the control tree and the 348 cases come from this baseline.

options.label: Use this baseline
options.description: Keep Android v5.3.5-nightly as the target for 5.4.0.
options.consequences: The requirement set and all cases stay valid. A later Android change needs a new baseline.

options.label: Move to another baseline
options.description: Pick a different Android commit or version.
options.consequences: The extraction, the control tree and the case set must be rerun.

decisions.question: Should the 56 Android-only cases stay out of the HarmonyOS port?
decisions.reason: Some surfaces depend on Android platform APIs that the public HarmonyOS SDK does not expose.

options.label: Keep them out
options.description: Record each case as android-only with the platform reason.
options.consequences: The port does not spend time on surfaces it cannot ship. A HarmonyOS equivalent can be added later.

options.label: Find equivalents
options.description: Design a HarmonyOS substitute for each Android-only surface.
options.consequences: The scope grows. Some substitutes need product decisions and extra design work.

decisions.question: Do the 11 unit journeys match how a phone user works?
decisions.reason: Each journey drives one unit of implementation and its E2E cases.

options.label: Accept the journeys
options.description: Use the 11 unit journeys as the requirement-layer journeys.
options.consequences: Implementation and E2E can start per unit.

options.label: Rework named journeys
options.description: List the journeys that do not match real use.
options.consequences: The affected unit and its cases return to the requirement layer.

decisions.question: Is the 348-case set the right acceptance bar for 5.4.0?
decisions.reason: Every requirement item has at least one case, and every case has a parity tag.

options.label: Use all 348 cases
options.description: Treat every case as an acceptance check for the release.
options.consequences: The release is complete only when the portable cases pass and the android-only cases have a recorded decision.

options.label: Trim the set
options.description: Drop cases that are not worth automating or checking by hand.
options.consequences: The dropped requirements lose their acceptance evidence.

technical_notes.reason: Every requirement has at least one case

assumptions.statement: The pinned Android baseline is the intended parity target.
assumptions.basis: The user named the Android version in the same repository tree.
assumptions.consequence: A later Android change is out of scope until a new baseline is set.

assumptions.statement: Android-only surfaces stay Android-only unless HarmonyOS exposes an equivalent system API.
assumptions.basis: The public HarmonyOS SDK does not expose every Android platform surface.
assumptions.consequence: Some cases become platform decisions instead of implementation work.

assumptions.statement: A control that is visible but disabled still counts as a control.
assumptions.basis: The parity target is the visible UI, not only the active paths.
assumptions.consequence: Disabled controls stay in the tree and in the case set.
